newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end lower, golds lose shine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end lower, golds lose shine.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2406 -8 US 30yr cl 6.42 +0.01

*Stocks end weaker, golds lead losers, BHP retraces some recent gains, banks help limit losses. Volume 368.09 million shares, value A$653.15 million, 1,095 stocks traded, 333 steady, 322 up, 440 down.
Australian shares closed weaker on Friday as market leader BHP retraced some of its recent gains and gold miners followed the gold price to lower ground.

National Australia Bank proved to be the star of the show, its shares cracking a record high of A$14.42 as buyers voiced their approval of Thursday's 6.8 percent higher full year net profit of A$2.1 billion.
At 4.30 p.m. (0530 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was down 9.1 points at 2,383.4. December share price index futures were eight points lower at 2,406 and were at an 22.6 point premium to the index.
"BHP came off again in the afternoon and the golds were hit after the price drop but the rest just muddled along," said a Sydney broker, saying National Australia bank was a standout.
"National Australia Bank had a good result Thursday and that helped the banks along."
Miner CRA followed its dual listed twin RTZ Corp Plc into firmer territory, gaining five cents to A$20.05 in an overall weaker resources sector.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Both futures and options trading slowed up in a quiet pre-weekend session.
Total options traded 29,928 (42,852)
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 5,055 (10,494)

In other local markets, Australian bonds resumed the heady rally spanning the past 2-1/2 months as the short-end of the market saw the buoyancy of the local currency increasing the chances of a policy easing, analysts said.
Three-year bond yields made a clean break below 6.50 percent, but while long bond yields touched new 33-month lows at one stage, solid resistance remains at 7.0 percent.
By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.05 percent.

The Australian dollar stepped back a little Friday from the dizzying heights reached offshore but still looked well placed to extend its bull run. Some profit taking did emerge today after Thursday's impulsive rush ahead but the pullback was slight and dealers expected US$0.8050 to hold for a tilt at US$0.8150 next week.
By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT) the local dollar had edged back to US$0.8084/89 after suffering a touch of vertigo its US$0.8125 offshore peak but was still well up on Thursday's US$.8080/85.
